reason: 'in the words of the brahmasūtras (brahmasūtra-pada), which give reasons … and are decisive' made the compound a plural 'brahmasūtras' and let the two adjectives attach to it — close to the 'words of the Brahma-sūtra' rendering that the skeleton decision on 13.3-4 (700-verse numbering) corrects as one commentator's (Rāmānuja's) gloss — while the entry's notes say the paraphrase leaves the compound untranslated. hetumadbhir viniścitaiḥ agree with -padaiḥ ('words'). Now 'in the brahmasūtra words (brahmasūtra-pada), which give reasons (hetumat) and are decisive (viniścita)', as the chapter entry already has it.

acetas was rendered 'without awareness' and the notes said cetas is rendered 'awareness' as in the ch10-12 merge; the Gītā convention renders citta/cetas as 'thought (…)' (never 'mind'), as this chunk's own trm:cetas definition for this verse already does ('lack thought (acetas)'). Now 'without thought (acetas)'.

'from which the body arises' takes one of the two analyses of deha-samudbhava ('from which the body arises', as the commentators take it, or 'arising in/with the body'); the teaching 14.20 keeps the compound open, as the skeleton decision on 14.19-20 notes. Aligned with 14.20.

The definition dropped the verse's 'also' (kṣetrajñaṃ cāpi māṃ viddhi, 13.3), on which the readings recorded in dsp:bhagavad-gita-ksetrajna-and-the-lord turn (the teaching 13.3 notes: 'the verse says only that the Lord is "also" (api) to be known as the knower in all fields'). Restored.

'the removal of doubt' was given, unattributed, as a sense of apohana; it is not the verse's word, and the readings the teaching 15.15 records (labelled as the commentators') are the loss of memory and knowledge and reasoning that excludes (ūha-apoha). Aligned with 15.15 and trm:apohana.

14.19 makes the attainment of the Lord's state follow on two things — seeing no agent other than the guṇas and knowing what is higher than the guṇas (guṇebhyaś ca paraṃ vetti); the definition kept only the first, which changes what the verse conditions the result on. Restored, as cpt:gunas-as-agents has it.

The only senses recorded under this id in data/ are the haṭha/Upaniṣadic first stage of yoga (ārambha-avasthā); 14.12 and 14.25 use the ordinary word 'undertaking' (of actions). The definition now says so, as the ch10-12 check did for kleśa.

'seen only by those with the eye of knowledge' added 'only' and left out 15.11, where striving yogins also see it; the verses contrast the deluded, who do not see (15.10), with those with the eye of knowledge and striving yogins, who do (15.10–11).

'effects and instruments (kārya-kāraṇa)' renders the variant kārya-karaṇa ('effect and instruments', the body and the faculties in Śaṅkara's gloss), but this edition reads kārya-kāraṇa, 'effect and cause' — as the teaching 13.21 and cpt:prakrti here render it, and as the skeleton decisions on 13.19-23 and 13.19-20 (700-verse numbering) correct in the skeleton.
